reason: Legacy silently drops a `delete` step whose eid is a ref lookup (`lookup("primaryOwner.id", <uuid>)`): admin/model.clj expand-delete emits [:delete-entity [attr value] etype], transaction.clj resolve-lookups-for-delete-entity only keeps steps whose lookup resolved through resolve-lookups, and that resolution comes back empty for ref attrs on the live server (verified: the doc stays, tx-id is still returned; plain lookups and the same ref lookup on update/merge/link all resolve). This server resolves ref lookups with the same resolver for every op, so the delete happens. The admin SDK only reads tx-id from the response either way; the divergence is the entity surviving, which is the legacy defect, not a wire shape.

reason: Hardening (issue #38 item 11). Legacy's deny-redirect! deletes the redirect by id before it checks anything and never compares the grant token, so a deny with a wrong grant token succeeds and a deny with a wrong cookie still burns the redirect (the real deny that follows is then record-not-found). This server checks the grant token (record-not-found, like grant) and the cookie before deleting, so the rightful deny after either bad attempt still redirects with access_denied.

reason: Decided divergence: legacy's reject-by-id-and-foreign-key formats the id-only query (reject-by-id-qs) against the route's invite table, so an org admin revoking through their own org's path revokes a pending invite of any other org by id (probed with an invite of a second org, revoked through the team org's path; an app invite revoked through an org path stays pending on both servers because the org table has no such id). This server scopes the revoke to the org in the path, so the other org's invite stays pending. docs/PARITY.md (wire-level divergences: invite revoke scope).

reason: `data.title.endsWith('a')` errors on a row without a title. This server, like legacy with the flag off, fails the whole query with `permission-evaluation-failed` (one erroring view rule fails the query). With the flag on, legacy's rewriter turns the rule into `{title: {$like: '%a'}}`, the title-less row never matches, and the matched rows skip the per-entity check, so legacy answers. Rule evaluation stays per entity here, so a rule that errors on some row keeps failing the query, as on a default legacy server. Only with the operator's `rule-wheres` flag listing the app (off by default on a self-hosted server; this layer turns it on for its own app). With the flag off legacy answers like this server (the rulewheres:flag-off/ comparisons of the same queries match).

reason: Legacy bug, and it over-shares: `_datakey_starts_with` puts the CEL prefix into the LIKE pattern unescaped (cel.clj:1328), so `data.title.startsWith('a_')` becomes `$like 'a_%'` and `_` matches any character. Rows the rule denies (`alpha`, `alphas`) are shown to the guest, and the matched rows skip the per-entity check that would have denied them. This server evaluates `startsWith` per entity and shows only `a_c`. Only with the operator's `rule-wheres` flag listing the app (off by default on a self-hosted server; this layer turns it on for its own app). With the flag off legacy answers like this server (the rulewheres:flag-off/ comparisons of the same queries match).
